rationale: Accepted: the critique's main points. (1) base_speed 1.6 was an unverified PWM guess, so I lower it to 1.5 (75% PWM). This keeps the speed needed for completion but adds margin against off-track exits on tight bends. (2) The critique is right that there is no slowing mechanism, and base_pwm is constant. I accept that and do not claim slowing; I rely on the lower base speed and the forward sensors for bends. (3) Signal is a normalised weighted average, so I raise kp from 3 to 3.5 to get a stronger correction at typical tape-edge signals (about 0.3 to 0.6), not the extreme value of 1. (4) Derivative noise: I cut kd from 0.5 to 0.15. Noise of about 2% per step gives derivative terms of roughly 0.3 turn units (about 100 PWM) instead of about 1 unit, so the derivative stays a damper and does not amplify noise. (5) Sensor coverage: I move the sensor row forward to y=0.06 (from 0.04). Sensors see the line earlier, which offsets the steering lag at higher speed. Lateral spread stays at plus or minus 0.04 m with 0.02 m spacing, because the 25 mm tape plus 12 mm footprints still gives one or two sensors on the line for offsets up to about 0.04 m. (6) ki stays at 0.05. It is nearly inert but harmless, and I do not claim it removes a measured steady-state error. (7) body_width stays at 0.12 (the off-track limit is 0.06 m regardless), and I drop the claim that the body size matters. (8) Line-loss recovery stays at last_direction, which turns toward the side the line was last seen. Rejected: the critique's suggestion of a conservative start at much lower speed. Completion within 3 s needs real speed, so 1.5 is the compromise. Expected result: completion on the oval and s-bend, with the most risk on the slalom. Decision rule for the next iteration: if line_loss_events is above 2 or max_error exceeds 0.05, lower base_speed by 0.1. If completion is 0 with progress above 0.9, raise base_speed by 0.1. If steering_oscillation is high with rms_error low, lower kp. If rms_error is high with no oscillation, raise kp.
